_meta.what_this_is: A teacher model's soft output distributions over four classes for several training examples. Each distribution is what the teacher actually produces (a probability per class); the hard label is just its argmax. Three of the examples are all argmax 'cat' but with very different distributions -- a confident cat, a barely-a-cat, and a cat easily confused with a car -- so hard labels collapse the three into one identical target while the soft targets keep them distinct. This is the setup for distillation: train the student on the soft distributions, not the hard labels.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The soft distributions are hand-authored (each sums to 1) so the dark-knowledge mass, runner-up classes, entropies, and the collapsed group are exact and checkable; every quantity is computed in distill.py. e1/e2/e3 share the hard label 'cat' but differ; e3's runner-up is 'car' where e1/e2's is 'dog'.
_meta.format: classes: the class names in index order; examples: [{id, soft}] where soft is the teacher's probability per class.
